name: Street Corn Chicken Rice Bowl

ingredients.buy: 2/3 cup crumbled; 1/2 cup crumbled, for topping
juice and zest of 3 1/2 limes; 7 tablespoons
1/2 cup chopped; 2/3 cup chopped; 1 1/2 cups leaves, for topping

writer_notes: Batch is a clean 3.5x scale of the 4-serving source (14/4). Every locked quantity matches that factor; chicken 4 3/4 lb sits inside the scaled 4.375-5.25 lb window.
Cotija 2/3 cup = 3 Tbsp x3.5 (10.5 vs 10.67 Tbsp per 2/3 cup); rounds clean, no concern.

prose.intro_html:
Mexican street corn, elote, is one of those things that tastes like a special occasion and costs like a Tuesday. We took everything good about it, the creamy lime corn, the salty cotija, the little kick of jalapeno, and built a full dinner around it. Grilled-style chicken, cilantro lime rice, and a scoop of that street corn salad on top. It eats like a food truck order and preps like a champion.

Here is the part your budget will like. This bowl lands at {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein per serving, so it clears our high-protein bar without a protein powder in sight. Real chicken, real rice, real corn. You cook once and you eat like this all week.
prose.shop_smart:
Buy the chicken breast in the biggest pack that fits your freezer, because this batch wants close to five pounds and per-pound the family pack is where the value lives. Cut it into one-inch chunks yourself instead of paying for pre-cut strips.

Canned whole kernel corn is the move here. It is already cooked, you just drain and stir, and it holds its price steady all year long while fresh corn swings with the season. Grab enough cans to cover seven cups drained.

Cotija is a hard, salty crumbling cheese, and a little goes a long way across fourteen bowls, so one wedge covers both the salad and the topping. If your store does not carry it, a firm feta crumbles the same way. Buy your limes whole for the juice and the zest, skip the little squeeze bottles, and pick up your cilantro, jalapeno, avocado, and red onion fresh so the toppings taste bright.
prose.make_it:
Start the rice, because it runs on its own while you build everything else. Bring the water to a boil in a large pot, stir in the rice and the sea salt, then cover it, drop the heat to low, and let it simmer about twenty minutes until it is tender. While it cooks, stir together your chopped cilantro, lime juice, and lime zest in a big bowl. When the rice is done, fold it into that cilantro lime mix and set it aside.

Make the street corn salad next. In a bowl, combine the drained corn, Greek yogurt, cotija, mayo, lime juice and zest, the diced jalapeno if you want the heat, cilantro, and salt. Stir it gently until it comes together and taste it, then set it aside to let the flavors get to know each other.

Now the chicken. Combine the chili powder, sea salt, cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder, and onion powder in a small bowl, then toss the chicken chunks in that spice blend until every piece is coated. Get the olive oil hot in a large skillet over medium heat, add the chicken, and cook it about four to five minutes per side until it is cooked through and the internal temp hits 165 degrees. Work in batches if your skillet crowds, because crowded chicken steams instead of browning.

To build, lay down the warm cilantro lime rice, top it with the chicken, add a generous scoop of the street corn, then finish with avocado, red onion, a little more cotija and cilantro, and a squeeze of fresh lime.
prose.portion_html:
This batch fills fourteen containers, so let the scale do the dividing instead of your eyeballs. Weigh the pot of rice empty first, or note the total cooked weight, then split it into fourteen even portions across your containers. Do the same with the chicken and the street corn. Even portions mean every single lunch hits the same {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein, no lucky containers and no sad ones.

Keep the avocado, red onion, and that final squeeze of lime as fresh add-ons rather than packing them in. Avocado browns and onion loses its snap after a few days, so store the rice, chicken, and corn together and crown each bowl the morning you eat it.
prose.cost_closing_html:
Here is what matters at the register. This whole thing comes out to ${{cost_ps}} per serving, and for that you get a real chicken-and-rice dinner with a street corn upgrade on top. Try ordering elote chicken bowls from a food truck fourteen times and see what your card statement thinks about that.

The math works because the expensive-sounding parts, the cotija and the lime and the fresh herbs, are stretched across fourteen bowls where a pinch each is all it takes. The chicken, rice, and corn carry the volume, and those are three of the cheapest ways to eat well that exist.

Eat this instead of takeout even a couple nights a week and the savings pay for the ingredients and then some. That is the whole point of cooking once and eating all week.
prose.upsell_html: If a plan that turns street corn cravings into fourteen paid-for lunches sounds like your kind of thing, the whole Thrifty Crew library runs you a dollar a month. That is less than the lime you squeezed on top. Come cook the rest of the week with us.

head.description: Street Corn Chicken Rice Bowls: seasoned chicken, cilantro lime rice, and creamy Mexican street corn salad. A budget high-protein meal prep dinner that scales to 14 servings.
head.keywords: street corn chicken bowls, elote chicken rice bowl, high protein meal prep, chicken rice bowl meal prep, budget meal prep dinner, cilantro lime rice, mexican street corn salad
steps: Bring the water to a boil in a large pot, stir in the rice and sea salt, cover, reduce the heat to low, and simmer about 20 minutes until tender. Stir chopped cilantro with lime juice and lime zest in a bowl, then fold in the warm rice.
In a bowl, combine the drained corn, Greek yogurt, cotija, mayo, lime juice and zest, diced jalapeno if using, cilantro, and salt. Stir gently until combined, taste, and set aside.
Combine the chili powder, sea salt, cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder, and onion powder in a small bowl. Toss the one-inch chicken chunks in the spice blend until fully coated.

Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the chicken and cook about 4 to 5 minutes per side until cooked through and the internal temp reaches 165 degrees, working in batches if needed.
Divide the cilantro lime rice across the containers, then top each with chicken and a generous scoop of the street corn salad.
Finish each bowl with cubed avocado, sliced red onion, extra cotija and cilantro, and a squeeze of fresh lime.
